Oakridge Unified School District Accessibility Standards and Procedures, Version 2024-03
Document type/version: policy document

1.1 Purpose. This document establishes the district-wide standards and procedures for accessibility of all facilities, programs, services, and activities operated or maintained by the Oakridge Unified School District (OUSD or the District). It is adopted by the Accessibility Compliance Committee pursuant to its authority under Board Policy 6220.

1.2 Scope. These standards apply to all District-owned, leased, or otherwise operated properties, including but not limited to school campuses, administrative offices, maintenance yards, and temporary structures. They also govern the conduct of District employees, contractors, and volunteers whose work affects the accessibility of District facilities or programs.

1.3 Authority. The Accessibility Compliance Committee is the approving body for this document and any subsequent revisions. The Committee shall review these standards on an annual basis and may adopt revisions at any time as required by changes in law, regulation, or District need.

1.4 Effective Date. This version takes effect on July 1, 2024. All prior versions are hereby superseded and shall no longer be cited as the governing standard for any purpose, including but not limited to inspection findings, work order prioritization, or annual reporting.

1.5 Severability. If any provision of this document is held invalid or unenforceable, the remainder shall continue in full force and effect.

---

SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 Accessible Route. A continuous, unobstructed path connecting all accessible elements and spaces of a building or facility that complies with the standards set forth in Section 3 of this document. Accessible routes include walks, curb ramps, ramps, elevators, and floor areas.

2.2 Alteration. A change to a facility that affects or could affect the usability of the facility or any part thereof. Alterations do not include normal maintenance, rereroofing, painting, wallpapering, or changes to mechanical and electrical systems unless those changes affect accessibility.

Oakridge Unified School District has_accessibility_policy_version 2024-03 version. Record status: current.

2.3 Barrier. Any condition that impedes the full and equal access of individuals with disabilities to programs, services, or activities, including physical, architectural, communication, or policy-related barriers.

2.4 Committee. The Accessibility Compliance Committee established by Board Policy 6220, responsible for the adoption, maintenance, and enforcement of these standards.

2.5 Facility. All or any portion of a building, structure, site, complex, or other real property, including the site where the building is located.

2.6 Inspection. A documented review of a facility or portion thereof conducted to identify compliance with these standards, performed by a qualified inspector designated by the Committee.

2.7 Program Access. The requirement that each program, service, or activity, when viewed in its entirety, be readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities. Program access may be achieved through structural means, policy changes, or provision of auxiliary aids and services, as determined appropriate by the Committee.

2.8 Qualified Inspector. An individual who has completed the District's accessibility inspection training and has been certified by the Committee to conduct inspections. Certification shall be renewed every two years.

2.9 Significant Barrier. A barrier that prevents a person with a disability from accessing a core program or service, or that poses a direct threat to health or safety. Significant barriers shall be given priority in the remediation process.

2.10 Work Order. A written or electronic request for corrective action, generated as a result of an inspection finding or other report, and tracked through the District's maintenance management system.
3.0 General Facility Standards

3.1 Application. The standards in this section apply to all facilities owned, leased, or operated by the District, including administrative offices, school sites, maintenance yards, and any temporary structures used for instructional or administrative purposes. Facilities constructed or altered after the effective date of these standards shall comply with the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, as adopted and incorporated herein by reference. Existing facilities shall be brought into compliance through the District's Transition Plan, updated annually and submitted to the Committee by September 30 of each year.

3.2 Paths of Travel. A path of travel shall be provided from facility entrances to all primary function areas, including classrooms, cafeterias, libraries, gymnasiums, administrative offices, and assembly spaces. The path of travel shall be at least 36 inches wide at all points, with passing spaces of at least 60 inches by 60 inches provided at reasonable intervals not to exceed 200 feet. Where the path of travel exceeds 200 feet in length, a resting area with a bench or other seating shall be provided. Changes in level along the path of travel shall not exceed 1/2 inch without a ramp or curb ramp. Changes in level between 1/4 inch and 1/2 inch shall be beveled with a slope not steeper than 1:2.

3.3 Surface Conditions. The surface of the path of travel shall be firm, stable, and slip-resistant. Loose gravel, sand, or other unstable materials shall not be used as the primary surface of a path of travel. Carpet and carpet tile shall be securely attached, with a maximum pile height of 1/2 inch, and exposed edges shall have trim on all sides. The vertical clearance along the path of travel shall be at least 80 inches, measured from the finished floor or ground surface. Protruding objects shall not reduce this clearance; where objects protrude from walls with their leading edges between 27 inches and 80 inches above the finished floor, they shall not protrude more than 4 inches into the path of travel. Objects mounted on posts or pylons may protrude any amount where the clear floor space required for the object is provided.

3.4 Ramps. Ramps shall have a running slope between 1:20 and 1:12, except that ramps serving existing facilities may have a running slope of up to 1:10 where compliance with the 1:12 maximum slope is not technically feasible, as determined by a qualified inspector and documented in the inspection report. The cross slope of ramp surfaces shall not exceed 1:48. Ramps shall have a clear width of at least 36 inches between handrails, and shall have edge protection on both sides where the ramp surface is not level with the adjacent surface. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches shall have handrails on both sides, mounted between 34 inches and 38 inches above the ramp surface, and shall extend horizontally at least 12 inches beyond the top and bottom of the ramp run. Landings shall be at least 60 inches long and at least as wide as the widest ramp run leading to the landing. Where ramps change direction between runs, the landing shall be at least 60 inches by 60 inches. Level landings shall be provided at the top and bottom of each ramp run, with a slope not exceeding 1:48 in any direction.

3.5 Curb Ramps. Curb ramps shall be provided wherever a pedestrian path of travel crosses a curb. Each curb ramp shall have a running slope between 1:12 and 1:10, a cross slope of 1:48 maximum, and a clear width of at least 36 inches, exclusive of flared sides. The transition from the curb ramp to the street, gutter, or roadway shall be flush, with no vertical change in level. The ramp shall be oriented so that the slope aligns with the direction of pedestrian travel. Where a curb ramp is provided at a marked crossing, the ramp shall be wholly contained within the markings. Diagonal curb ramps shall have a clear space of at least 48 inches by 48 inches at the top of the ramp, entirely outside the parallel vehicle travel lane.

**Section 4 — Inspection Scheduling and Documentation**

4.1 Inspection Cycle. All district facilities, including school sites, administrative offices, and support buildings, shall be inspected for compliance with these Standards at least once every three years. The Assistant Superintendent of Facilities shall maintain a rolling inspection calendar that ensures no facility goes longer than 36 months between inspections. Newly acquired or newly constructed facilities shall receive an initial baseline inspection within 90 days of occupancy. Facilities that have undergone a renovation or alteration affecting an accessible route, parking, or an entrance shall be re-inspected within 60 days of the completion of the work.

4.2 Annual Self-Evaluation. In addition to the triennial compliance inspection, each school site shall conduct an annual self-evaluation of its parking, paths of travel, ramps, curb ramps, entrances, and doorways using the checklist provided in Appendix C of these Standards. The site administrator shall complete the self-evaluation by May 1 of each year and submit it to the Accessibility Compliance Committee. The self-evaluation is a preliminary screening tool and does not substitute for a formal inspection by a qualified inspector.

4.3 Qualified Inspectors. Formal compliance inspections shall be conducted by a qualified inspector, defined as an individual with demonstrated training or certification in accessibility standards, including but not limited to the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessibility Guidelines (ADAAG) and the California Building Code, Chapter 11B. The district may use its own trained staff or contract with an outside consultant. All inspectors, whether district staff or consultants, shall be approved by the Accessibility Compliance Committee prior to conducting an inspection.

4.4 Inspection Scheduling. The Accessibility Compliance Committee shall issue an annual inspection schedule by September 1 of each year, identifying the facilities to be inspected during the upcoming fiscal year. The schedule shall be distributed to the affected site administrators no fewer than 30 days before the first scheduled inspection. Site administrators shall cooperate with the inspector, providing access to all areas of the facility, including mechanical rooms, storage areas, and temporary structures. If a scheduled inspection cannot be completed due to lack of access, the inspector shall document the missed area and reschedule within 15 business days.

4.5 Inspection Report Requirements. Each inspection shall result in a written report, prepared on the district’s standard Inspection Report form. The report shall include, at a minimum:

a) The date and time of the inspection and the name and title of the qualified inspector;

b) The name and address of the facility inspected;

c) A list of all areas and elements inspected, with a notation of whether each element was compliant, non-compliant, or not applicable;

d) A description of each non-compliance, including its location, the standard violated (by section number of these Standards), and a measurement or other factual basis for the finding;

e) Photographs of each non-compliance, taken in a manner that clearly documents the condition, with the photograph number referenced in the corresponding finding; and

f) A summary of the findings, including the total number of non-compliant items and a preliminary classification of each item as either a priority item requiring immediate correction or a non-priority item to be addressed during the next scheduled maintenance cycle.

1.1 Purpose. This document establishes the district-wide standards and procedures for accessibility of all facilities, programs, services, and activities operated or maintained by the Oakridge Unified School District (OUSD or the District). It is adopted by the Accessibility Compliance Committee pursuant to its authority under Board Policy 6220.

1.2 Scope. These standards apply to all District-owned, leased, or otherwise operated properties, including but not limited to school campuses, administrative offices, maintenance yards, and temporary structures. They also govern the conduct of District employees, contractors, and volunteers whose work affects the accessibility of District facilities or programs.

1.3 Authority. The Accessibility Compliance Committee is the approving body for this document and any subsequent revisions. The Committee shall review these standards on an annual basis and may adopt revisions at any time as required by changes in law, regulation, or District need.

1.4 Effective Date. This version takes effect on July 1, 2024. All prior versions are hereby superseded and shall no longer be cited as the governing standard for any purpose, including but not limited to inspection findings, work order prioritization, or annual reporting.

1.5 Severability. If any provision of this document is held invalid or unenforceable, the remainder shall continue in full force and effect.

---

SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 Accessible Route. A continuous, unobstructed path connecting all accessible elements and spaces of a building or facility that complies with the standards set forth in Section 3 of this document. Accessible routes include walks, curb ramps, ramps, elevators, and floor areas.

2.2 Alteration. A change to a facility that affects or could affect the usability of the facility or any part thereof. Alterations do not include normal maintenance, rereroofing, painting, wallpapering, or changes to mechanical and electrical systems unless those changes affect accessibility.

2.3 Barrier. Any condition that impedes the full and equal access of individuals with disabilities to programs, services, or activities, including physical, architectural, communication, or policy-related barriers.

2.4 Committee. The Accessibility Compliance Committee established by Board Policy 6220, responsible for the adoption, maintenance, and enforcement of these standards.

2.5 Facility. All or any portion of a building, structure, site, complex, or other real property, including the site where the building is located.

2.6 Inspection. A documented review of a facility or portion thereof conducted to identify compliance with these standards, performed by a qualified inspector designated by the Committee.

2.7 Program Access. The requirement that each program, service, or activity, when viewed in its entirety, be readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities. Program access may be achieved through structural means, policy changes, or provision of auxiliary aids and services, as determined appropriate by the Committee.

2.8 Qualified Inspector. An individual who has completed the District's accessibility inspection training and has been certified by the Committee to conduct inspections. Certification shall be renewed every two years.

2.9 Significant Barrier. A barrier that prevents a person with a disability from accessing a core program or service, or that poses a direct threat to health or safety. Significant barriers shall be given priority in the remediation process.

3.0 General Facility Standards

3.1 Application. The standards in this section apply to all facilities owned, leased, or operated by the District, including administrative offices, school sites, maintenance yards, and any temporary structures used for instructional or administrative purposes. Facilities constructed or altered after the effective date of these standards shall comply with the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, as adopted and incorporated herein by reference. Existing facilities shall be brought into compliance through the District's Transition Plan, updated annually and submitted to the Committee by September 30 of each year.

3.2 Paths of Travel. A path of travel shall be provided from facility entrances to all primary function areas, including classrooms, cafeterias, libraries, gymnasiums, administrative offices, and assembly spaces. The path of travel shall be at least 36 inches wide at all points, with passing spaces of at least 60 inches by 60 inches provided at reasonable intervals not to exceed 200 feet. Where the path of travel exceeds 200 feet in length, a resting area with a bench or other seating shall be provided. Changes in level along the path of travel shall not exceed 1/2 inch without a ramp or curb ramp. Changes in level between 1/4 inch and 1/2 inch shall be beveled with a slope not steeper than 1:2.

3.3 Surface Conditions. The surface of the path of travel shall be firm, stable, and slip-resistant. Loose gravel, sand, or other unstable materials shall not be used as the primary surface of a path of travel. Carpet and carpet tile shall be securely attached, with a maximum pile height of 1/2 inch, and exposed edges shall have trim on all sides. The vertical clearance along the path of travel shall be at least 80 inches, measured from the finished floor or ground surface. Protruding objects shall not reduce this clearance; where objects protrude from walls with their leading edges between 27 inches and 80 inches above the finished floor, they shall not protrude more than 4 inches into the path of travel. Objects mounted on posts or pylons may protrude any amount where the clear floor space required for the object is provided.

3.4 Ramps. Ramps shall have a running slope between 1:20 and 1:12, except that ramps serving existing facilities may have a running slope of up to 1:10 where compliance with the 1:12 maximum slope is not technically feasible, as determined by a qualified inspector and documented in the inspection report. The cross slope of ramp surfaces shall not exceed 1:48. Ramps shall have a clear width of at least 36 inches between handrails, and shall have edge protection on both sides where the ramp surface is not level with the adjacent surface. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches shall have handrails on both sides, mounted between 34 inches and 38 inches above the ramp surface, and shall extend horizontally at least 12 inches beyond the top and bottom of the ramp run. Landings shall be at least 60 inches long and at least as wide as the widest ramp run leading to the landing. Where ramps change direction between runs, the landing shall be at least 60 inches by 60 inches. Level landings shall be provided at the top and bottom of each ramp run, with a slope not exceeding 1:48 in any direction.

3.5 Curb Ramps. Curb ramps shall be provided wherever a pedestrian path of travel crosses a curb. Each curb ramp shall have a running slope between 1:12 and 1:10, a cross slope of 1:48 maximum, and a clear width of at least 36 inches, exclusive of flared sides. The transition from the curb ramp to the street, gutter, or roadway shall be flush, with no vertical change in level. The ramp shall be oriented so that the slope aligns with the direction of pedestrian travel. Where a curb ramp is provided at a marked crossing, the ramp shall be wholly contained within the markings. Diagonal curb ramps shall have a clear space of at least 48 inches by 48 inches at the top of the ramp, entirely outside the parallel vehicle travel lane.

**Oakridge Unified School District**
**Accessibility Compliance Committee**
**Accessibility Standards and Procedures, Version 2024-03**
**Adopted July 1, 2024**

**Section 4 — Inspection Scheduling and Documentation**

4.1 Inspection Cycle. All district facilities, including school sites, administrative offices, and support buildings, shall be inspected for compliance with these Standards at least once every three years. The Assistant Superintendent of Facilities shall maintain a rolling inspection calendar that ensures no facility goes longer than 36 months between inspections. Newly acquired or newly constructed facilities shall receive an initial baseline inspection within 90 days of occupancy. Facilities that have undergone a renovation or alteration affecting an accessible route, parking, or an entrance shall be re-inspected within 60 days of the completion of the work.

4.2 Annual Self-Evaluation. In addition to the triennial compliance inspection, each school site shall conduct an annual self-evaluation of its parking, paths of travel, ramps, curb ramps, entrances, and doorways using the checklist provided in Appendix C of these Standards. The site administrator shall complete the self-evaluation by May 1 of each year and submit it to the Accessibility Compliance Committee. The self-evaluation is a preliminary screening tool and does not substitute for a formal inspection by a qualified inspector.

4.3 Qualified Inspectors. Formal compliance inspections shall be conducted by a qualified inspector, defined as an individual with demonstrated training or certification in accessibility standards, including but not limited to the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessibility Guidelines (ADAAG) and the California Building Code, Chapter 11B. The district may use its own trained staff or contract with an outside consultant. All inspectors, whether district staff or consultants, shall be approved by the Accessibility Compliance Committee prior to conducting an inspection.

4.4 Inspection Scheduling. The Accessibility Compliance Committee shall issue an annual inspection schedule by September 1 of each year, identifying the facilities to be inspected during the upcoming fiscal year. The schedule shall be distributed to the affected site administrators no fewer than 30 days before the first scheduled inspection. Site administrators shall cooperate with the inspector, providing access to all areas of the facility, including mechanical rooms, storage areas, and temporary structures. If a scheduled inspection cannot be completed due to lack of access, the inspector shall document the missed area and reschedule within 15 business days.

4.5 Inspection Report Requirements. Each inspection shall result in a written report, prepared on the district’s standard Inspection Report form. The report shall include, at a minimum:

a) The date and time of the inspection and the name and title of the qualified inspector;

b) The name and address of the facility inspected;

#### 3.2 Highlighted Issues

The following issues were identified as priority concerns during the reporting period:

- **Westwood Elementary School – Main Entry Ramp:** The ramp slope was measured at 9.2% (1:10.9), exceeding the allowable maximum of 8.3% (1:12). The ramp also lacked a level landing at the top. A work order was issued in March 2024; reconstruction is scheduled for the summer break.

- **Lincoln Middle School – Restroom 112:** The grab bar adjacent to the toilet was mounted at 36 inches above the floor, which is within the acceptable range; however, the clearance between the grab bar and the wall was measured at 1.25 inches, below the required 1.5 inches. The bar was also noted to be loose at the rear anchor point. Corrective action was completed on May 3, 2024.

- **Fremont High School – Parking Lot B:** Two accessible parking spaces lacked the required access aisle, and the signage for one space was mounted at 48 inches to the centerline, exceeding the 60-inch maximum height. Both issues were corrected as of June 14, 2024.

- Madison Elementary – playground surface transition (work order issued June 2024)
- Jefferson High School – main entry door power assist (part on order; installation expected July 2024)

#### 4.2 Budget Variance

The original adopted budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 was $875,000. The final expenditures of $831,520 represent an underrun of $43,480 (5.0%). The variance is primarily attributable to lower-than-anticipated costs for the Lincoln Middle School restroom corrective work and the Fremont High School parking lot signage, both of which were completed without requiring replacement of underlying concrete or asphalt.

The unspent balance has been carried forward to the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget and is designated for the Roosevelt Middle School exterior stair handrail replacement and the Jefferson High School main entry door power assist installation.

---

### 5. Site-by-Site Summary

The following section provides a summary of inspection outcomes by school site. Each entry lists the date of the annual inspection, the number of violations cited, and the status of corrective actions as of June 30, 2024. Work order numbers refer to the district’s maintenance management system.

#### 5.1 Elementary Schools

**Adams Elementary** – Annual inspection: October 12, 2023. Two violations cited: (1) the accessible route from the parking lot to the main entrance had a cross-slope of 2.4%, exceeding the 2.0% maximum; (2) the door to the library had an opening force of 6.5 pounds, above the 5.0-pound maximum. Corrective action: Work order 2023-1147 was issued for the cross-slope repair; the door closer was adjusted on November 2, 2023. As of June 30, 2024, the cross-slope repair is complete; the door remains within acceptable force limits.

**Baker Elementary** – Annual inspection: November 28, 2023. One violation cited: the accessible parking space in the staff lot lacked the required 60-inch access aisle. Corrective action: Work order 2023-1201 was issued and completed on December 15, 2023, with striping and signage installed. No outstanding items.

**Carson Elementary** – Annual inspection: February 6, 2024. No violations cited. All accessible routes, restrooms, and playground surfaces were found to be in compliance.

Corrective action: Work order 2024-0318 was issued for the ramp repair; the fountain clear floor space was corrected by relocating a trash receptacle. Both items were verified as complete on April 10, 2024.

**Franklin Elementary** – Annual inspection: December 5, 2023. One violation cited: the handrail on the interior stairway at the north wing was installed at 35 inches above the stair nosing, below the required 34-38 inch range. documents.content:
**ACCESSIBILITY INSPECTION FORM**
**Westwood Elementary School**
**Inspection Date: June 15, 2024**

---

**SUMMARY OF FINDINGS**

This inspection covered accessibility compliance for Westwood Elementary School, located at 1400 Maple Grove Road. The inspection was conducted on June 15, 2024, by Maria Gonzalez, ADA Compliance Inspector. The inspection included a full walkthrough of the main building, the two portable classroom wings, the library, the gymnasium, the cafeteria, the administrative offices, and all exterior routes, parking areas, and playground facilities.

A total of 87 individual items were inspected across the categories listed in the sections above. Of these, 74 items were found to be in compliance (Pass), 11 items were found to be out of compliance (Fail), and 2 items were not applicable to this facility. A summary of the failed items is provided below, along with the corrective action status as of the date of this report.

**SUMMARY TABLE OF FAILED ITEMS**

| Item ID | Location | Description of Deficiency | Corrective Action / Status |
|---------|----------|---------------------------|----------------------------|
| A1c | Main entrance – north walkway | Ramp slope exceeds 1:12 maximum. Measured slope 1:10.2. | Work order WO-2024-0618 issued. Pending. |
| B2b | Boys' restroom Rm 114 | Grab bar on rear wall of accessible stall is loose; moves 1/2 in. when 50 lb. downward force applied. | Work order WO-2024-0622 issued. Pending. |
| B3d | Girls' restroom Rm 116 | Sink drain pipe not insulated; surface temperature measured 152°F during hot water run. | Work order WO-2024-0623 issued. Pending. |
| C1c | Library circulation desk | Service counter height 42 in.; no auxiliary writing surface at accessible height. | Work order WO-2024-0625 issued. Pending. |
| D2b | Cafeteria serving line | Tray slide height 36 in.; requires 34 in. maximum per standard. | Work order WO-2024-0626 issued. Pending. |
| E1b | Portable classroom P-2 | Door threshold height 1 in.; exceeds 1/2 in. maximum. | Work order WO-2024-0627 issued. Pending. |
| F2a | Playground – south zone | Surface material under swings compacted; measured 2.1 in. depth of unitary surface, below 3 in. minimum. | Work order WO-2024-0629 issued. Pending. |
| G1c | Parking lot – accessible space 3 | Access aisle cross slope measured 2.4%; exceeds 2.0% maximum. | Work order WO-2024-0631 issued. Pending. |
| R2e | North walkway – exterior directional sign | Sign not illuminated. Photometric reading 0.8 fc at 9:15 PM. | Work order WO-2024-0633 issued. Pending. |
| R3d | Room 108 and Room 112 | Evacuation route maps not posted. | Work order WO-2024-0634 issued. Pending. |
| G3b | Drop-off zone – curb ramp | Curb ramp landing at top has 1.2% running slope; exceeds 1.5% maximum in direction of travel. | Work order WO-2024-0636 issued. Pending. |

**CORRECTIVE ACTION ITEMS**

The following corrective actions were recommended during the inspection and have been assigned to the Facilities Department. The work order numbers are referenced above and are tracked in the district's maintenance management system. The estimated completion dates are based on the priority assigned by the Facilities Supervisor.

1. **Ramp slope correction (A1c)** – The north walkway ramp must be rebuilt to achieve a maximum running slope of 1:12. The current measured slope of 1:10.2 exceeds the allowable maximum. The ramp is the primary accessible route from the staff parking lot to the main entrance. Temporary signage directing users to the alternate accessible entrance at the east side of the building should be posted until repairs are completed. Work order WO-2024-0618 has been assigned to the concrete contractor. Estimated completion: July 8, 2024.
